summary: A staged command-review pipeline combining shell rules, a lightweight classifier, BM25-ranked history, and LiteLLM before an allow, warn, or block decision.

architecture.title: Local interception
architecture.detail: A Typer CLI submits the command and user context to a local review API. Warn decisions require the literal CONFIRM response; block decisions exit before execution.

architecture.title: Layered analysis
architecture.detail: The engine short-circuits rules above 0.9 risk, then combines classifier risk, a history anomaly signal, and an LLM assessment. BM25 selects five relevant actions from up to 100 recent records filtered by user.

architecture.title: Recorded decisions
architecture.detail: SQLite stores commands, timestamps, risk scores, decisions, user confirmation, intent, and serialized context for the next review.

decisions.title: Critical signals survive averaging
decisions.detail: The scoring function preserves the highest individual rule, classifier, or LLM risk when it exceeds 0.8. Decision thresholds are greater than 0.7 for block and greater than 0.4 for warn.

decisions.title: Context stays bounded
decisions.detail: History retrieval uses shell-tokenized commands and BM25 rather than appending the entire command log to every LLM call. LLM contribution scales with its reported confidence.

contracts.name: analyze_action(command, user, context)
contracts.detail: Returns risk_score, intent, decision, reason, and confidence.

contracts.name: allow / warn / block
contracts.detail: The interceptor translates analysis into execution behavior, with explicit confirmation for warn.

scope: This is an alpha review tool. The current interceptor allows execution if its local API is unreachable or times out, so it is an advisory layer rather than a mandatory security boundary.

summary: A browser extension that turns visible DOM text and OCR into extractive answers, with IndexedDB caching and a local request monitor.

architecture.title: Structured page extraction
architecture.detail: A DOM TreeWalker skips scripts, styles, and hidden elements while collecting text. Separate paths gather viewport-adjacent content, document metadata, and table rows.

architecture.title: OCR off the page thread
architecture.detail: A Comlink-exposed OCR worker wraps Tesseract.js and returns recognized text with OCR confidence. IndexedDB stores page contexts and model-related cache records.

architecture.title: Extractive Q&A
architecture.detail: QAEngine classifies questions as summary, extraction, specific, or general, then scores and selects sentences from the page context. Timing markers cover processing and answer generation.

decisions.title: Local context is the core
decisions.detail: The implementation does not require a FastAPI or Redis service. Its privacy monitor wraps fetch and XMLHttpRequest, permits extension/blob URLs and local hosts, and rejects other absolute hosts in the monitored context.

decisions.title: Extraction before generation
decisions.detail: The implemented answer path uses sentence-selection heuristics. The model loader includes an ONNX integration placeholder; the current worker signals the main Q&A engine rather than running a downloaded model.

contracts.name: QAEngine.processQuestion(question)
contracts.detail: Produces questionId, text, confidence, isComplete, and timestamp.

contracts.name: recognizeText(imageData)
contracts.detail: Returns extracted text and OCR confidence from the worker.

scope: A prototype of local page understanding. The current heuristics are not a generative LLM, and the request monitor is not a complete extension-wide security sandbox.

summary: A Streamlit document assistant using recursive text splitting, MiniLM embeddings, persistent Chroma cosine search, document selection, and optional web-search augmentation.

architecture.title: Multi-format ingestion
architecture.detail: DocumentProcessor reads PDFs, Word documents, spreadsheets, JSON, CSV, Markdown, and text. Its default splitter uses 1,000-character chunks with 200-character overlap and preserves metadata.

architecture.title: Persistent semantic index
architecture.detail: VectorStore embeds chunks with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and stores them in a Chroma PersistentClient collection configured for cosine distance. Ingestion validates chunks, checks generated IDs, and adds records in batches.

architecture.title: Inspectable answer path
architecture.detail: RAGPipeline checks the query, retrieves candidates, applies selected-document filtering, optionally searches the web, and builds an answer with separate document and web source collections.

decisions.title: Evidence and answer travel together
decisions.detail: The result includes context quality, source records, guardrail warnings, and per-request metrics such as processing time and retrieved source counts. Those fields let the UI expose the route to an answer.

decisions.title: Selection filtering has a limit
decisions.detail: The pipeline retrieves twice the requested candidate count and then filters by selected filenames. A highly selective request can still return fewer passages than requested.

contracts.name: similarity_search(query, k=5)
contracts.detail: Retrieves document records, metadata, and relevance scores.

contracts.name: sources.documents / sources.web_results
contracts.detail: Keeps uploaded-document evidence separate from external search evidence.

scope: A public application implementation, not evidence of measured production throughput. Filename selection is a retrieval preference and should not be described as tenant authorization.

summary: A multi-language event collection system: HTTP and UDP ingestion in Go, Kafka transport, and a ClickHouse consumer with column-oriented event storage.

architecture.title: Two ingestion transports
architecture.detail: The collector accepts JSON at POST /api/v1/event and also listens for UDP datagrams. Missing event IDs and timestamps are filled with UUIDs and Unix milliseconds.

architecture.title: Kafka transport
architecture.detail: Events are serialized into the uamt-events topic through kafka-go. The consumer reads that topic with the clickhouse-consumer group and maps records into an events insert.

architecture.title: Analytical storage
architecture.detail: The ClickHouse events table uses MergeTree ordered by timestamp and event_type. A separate users table uses ReplacingMergeTree with updated_at as its version column.

decisions.title: Fast acknowledgment is not durable acknowledgment
decisions.detail: The HTTP collector responds 202 Accepted after launching a goroutine to publish the event. A later Kafka write failure is logged, so the acknowledgment does not prove durable delivery.

decisions.title: Storage is explicit and inspectable
decisions.detail: The schema separates event identity, session, event type, JSON metadata, and system attributes. The current consumer executes one insert per event rather than batching writes.

contracts.name: POST /api/v1/event → 202
contracts.detail: Returns received status and event_id.

contracts.name: events(event_id, timestamp, session_id, event_type, metadata, system_*)
contracts.detail: A stable event shape carried from collector to analytical storage.

scope: The repositories establish an ingestion architecture. Durable acknowledgments, insertion batching, and replay/deduplication guarantees would require further work before claiming production-grade delivery.

summary: A FastAPI and Next.js document-chat prototype with layered PDF extraction, OCR fallback, local embeddings, NumPy similarity search, and persisted source metadata.

architecture.title: Extraction fallbacks
architecture.detail: The backend tries multiple PDF extraction paths and can use pdf2image with pytesseract for scanned pages. The same service accepts document uploads and exposes audio transcription.

architecture.title: Local similarity search
architecture.detail: The preferred embedding model is all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Document vectors live in NumPy arrays; retrieval computes cosine similarity and selects up to five matching chunks.

architecture.title: File-based persistence
architecture.detail: Chunks and metadata are saved as JSON, while vector arrays are saved as compressed NPZ files. Source records associate retrieved chunks with document IDs and filenames.

decisions.title: A transparent index
decisions.detail: File-based NumPy storage makes the prototype easy to inspect without a vector database. Search scans the stored vectors rather than using an approximate-nearest-neighbor service.

decisions.title: Fallback quality must be visible
decisions.detail: The current code returns random vectors if the local embedding model is unavailable or embedding generation fails. That keeps the path executable but does not preserve meaningful semantic retrieval.

contracts.name: search_documents(query, top_k=5)
contracts.detail: Returns doc_id, filename, content, and score for selected chunks.

contracts.name: chunks.json / metadata.json / vectors.npz
contracts.detail: Persists the text, document mapping, and vector representations separately.

scope: A multimodal prototype with a clear improvement boundary: embedding failures should be surfaced explicitly before the retrieval result is trusted.

summary: A Next.js prompt workspace connected to FastAPI task APIs, Celery generation/evaluation workers, Redis result handling, and a saved prompt library.

architecture.title: Task-based frontend contract
architecture.detail: Server actions submit prompt-generation or evaluation work and receive a task ID and status URL. The frontend models PENDING, STARTED, SUCCESS, FAILURE, and RETRY states.

architecture.title: Background execution
architecture.detail: The published Python API defines separate generation and evaluation queues, JSON task serialization, late acknowledgment, and retrying Celery tasks. Redis Sentinel configuration resolves master and replica clients.

architecture.title: History and library
architecture.detail: The frontend database adapter uses PostgreSQL in production and a SQLite development fallback for local prompt history. Actions separate recent history from saved library entries and starring.

decisions.title: Long work has an identity
decisions.detail: A task URL lets the interface inspect progress independently of the initial submission. The backend caches successful task results and exposes failure states.

decisions.title: Public code is a separate artifact
decisions.detail: This repository contains a public prompt-workflow implementation. It is not presented as a published copy of UF IT’s internal NaviGator Prompt Builder deployment.

contracts.name: POST /prompts/generate
contracts.detail: Queues a generation task and returns task identification.

contracts.name: GET /prompts/task/{task_id}
contracts.detail: Reports background execution state and a result when available.

scope: The code demonstrates task APIs and persistence choices. Redis Sentinel configuration and retry settings alone do not prove a deployed high-availability topology or exactly-once execution.

summary: A Python CLI that downloads public incident PDFs, reconstructs wrapped records with regular expressions, inserts structured rows into SQLite, and reports grouped incident counts.

architecture.title: PDF-to-text boundary
architecture.detail: The download function returns PDF bytes through BytesIO. PyPDF2 extracts page text, while the parser skips report headers and identifies new incident lines by date.

architecture.title: Wrapped-record reconstruction
architecture.detail: A regular expression matches time, incident number, location, incident nature, and agency code. Continuation lines are joined to the preceding record for another parse attempt.

architecture.title: Relational output
architecture.detail: The incidents table has five text columns. Parameterized executemany inserts parsed rows; a GROUP BY query prints occurrence counts by incident nature.

decisions.title: A batch pipeline with clear stages
decisions.detail: The repository implements download, extraction, storage, and reporting. It does not implement a live event-stream processor despite the repository’s historical name.

decisions.title: Rebuild semantics
decisions.detail: Database setup drops and recreates the incidents table. A run replaces the table rather than providing an incremental ingestion or deduplication protocol.

contracts.name: fetchincidents → extractincidents → populatedb
contracts.detail: Separates transport, parsing, and storage functions.

contracts.name: incidents(time, number, location, nature, ori)
contracts.detail: Normalizes each extracted record into a queryable row.

scope: A format-specific incident ingestion project. Its parser relies on the report’s known incident and agency labels and should be reevaluated if the PDF layout changes.

summary: A Flask incident-analysis interface built on SQLite, pandas, OpenCage geocoding, KMeans clustering, and Matplotlib/Seaborn charts.

architecture.title: Tabular analysis
architecture.detail: The visualization module loads incident records into a pandas DataFrame and counts the most common incident natures.

architecture.title: Geographic projection
architecture.detail: Incident addresses are sent to OpenCage for coordinates. Rows without usable coordinates are removed before KMeans clustering over latitude and longitude.

architecture.title: Rendered chart artifacts
architecture.detail: Matplotlib and Seaborn export a top-20 incident bar chart, a geographic cluster plot, and a 24-hour incident distribution histogram for the Flask interface.

decisions.title: Charts are batch outputs
decisions.detail: The implementation produces image artifacts from a dataset snapshot. It is not a continuously updated live dashboard.

decisions.title: Missing coordinates affect the view
decisions.detail: Failed geocoding removes records from the clustering dataset, so the geographic view has a narrower population than the incident-frequency chart.

contracts.name: create_visualizations(db_path)
contracts.detail: Reads SQLite and writes bar_chart.png, clustering.png, and histogram.png.

contracts.name: geocode_address(address)
contracts.detail: Returns coordinates or an empty result for the spatial-analysis stage.

scope: A visualization project rather than a production incident service. Coordinate clustering is exploratory; it does not establish geographic distance-aware clustering or causal patterns.

summary: A small, explicit ETL command that reads FBI Wanted API pages or local JSON and normalizes records into a thorn-delimited text format.

architecture.title: Two input adapters
architecture.detail: The command accepts either --page for the FBI Wanted API or --file for a UTF-8 JSON file. HTTP errors propagate through requests.raise_for_status.

architecture.title: A normalization function
architecture.detail: process_data accepts an items envelope or a list of records. It normalizes subjects and field_offices into lists, handles missing values, and joins non-empty values.

architecture.title: Portable text output
architecture.detail: Each output line contains title, subjects, and field offices separated by the thorn character þ. The CLI writes the transformed records to standard output.

decisions.title: Keep transformation independent
decisions.detail: API access and file reading both feed the same normalization function. That makes processing behavior testable without a live HTTP request.

decisions.title: Be precise about the dataset
decisions.detail: The source is the FBI Wanted list API. This project is not a general FBI crime-statistics warehouse or a scheduled multi-source pipeline.

contracts.name: --page N / --file PATH
contracts.detail: Chooses a remote page or a local input artifact.

contracts.name: title þ subjects þ field_offices
contracts.detail: Defines the three-field output contract.

scope: A focused data-conversion project with tests for fetching and transformation. Pagination orchestration, retries, scheduling, and warehouse loading are outside the implemented CLI.

summary: A Flask resume-ranking workflow combining document extraction, sentence embeddings, TF-IDF similarity, structured skills, and job-description matching.

architecture.title: Document extraction
architecture.detail: The application uses PyPDF2 and docx2txt, with pdf2image and pytesseract available for scanned inputs. It parses resume content into structured fields.

architecture.title: Two matching signals
architecture.detail: SentenceTransformer embeddings provide cosine semantic similarity. A TF-IDF vectorizer provides a separate keyword similarity against the job description.

architecture.title: Structured ranking
architecture.detail: The ranker combines configured semantic and keyword weights with skills and other extracted signals. Results expose component scores rather than just a single unexplained number.

decisions.title: Lexical and semantic signals stay separate
decisions.detail: Exact terminology and paraphrased experience are different matching cases. Keeping their scores visible helps explain why a resume ranked the way it did.

decisions.title: Extraction quality affects matching
decisions.detail: OCR or parsing mistakes become inputs to both similarity paths. A confident-looking ranking should still be checked against the extracted document text.

contracts.name: calculate_similarity(resume_text, job_description)
contracts.detail: Returns semantic_score, keyword_score, and overall_score.

contracts.name: ResumeData / RankingResult
contracts.detail: Dataclasses organize extracted information and ranking components.

scope: A ranking tool for exploring fit against a job description. Its scores do not predict hiring decisions or establish compatibility with every employer’s applicant-tracking system.

summary: A supervised name-reconstruction experiment using redaction length, nearby words, part-of-speech features, n-grams, and a class-balanced logistic regression model.

architecture.title: Redaction-aware features
architecture.detail: The feature extractor counts block characters, locates the redacted token, and captures neighboring words, POS tags, sentence length, position, and local n-gram features.

architecture.title: Supervised classification
architecture.detail: Training rows are selected from a split-labeled TSV. CountVectorizer turns feature strings into sparse features, and LogisticRegression uses balanced class weights to predict name labels.

architecture.title: Validation and submission
architecture.detail: Validation computes weighted precision, recall, and F1. The test path generates a TSV containing record IDs and predicted names.

decisions.title: Study information leakage
decisions.detail: The experiment asks how much identity signal survives in surrounding text. It reconstructs redacted names; it does not detect and redact sensitive entities.

decisions.title: Feature engineering is inspectable
decisions.detail: Redaction length and adjacent POS features make the inputs explicit. The learned labels are drawn from the training set rather than generated as arbitrary names.

contracts.name: extract_features(context)
contracts.detail: Creates a feature string from masked text and its neighborhood.

contracts.name: submission.tsv: id, name
contracts.detail: Exports model predictions without changing the source documents.

scope: A supervised reconstruction experiment. No validated accuracy percentage is published here; repository metric display formatting is not treated as benchmark evidence.

summary: A Requests and BeautifulSoup scraper for UF job listings that pairs result rows with summaries and composes an email report.

architecture.title: Targeted HTML extraction
architecture.detail: The scraper fetches a filtered UF jobs page and locates the search-results-content table body. It processes alternating primary and summary rows.

architecture.title: Listing data shape
architecture.detail: Each listing carries title, link, department, location, closing date, and summary. The implementation returns the first 20 parsed jobs.

architecture.title: Message composition
architecture.detail: An SMTP path builds an email from the collected listings using environment-provided mail configuration. The script logs its run and invokes the scraper once from its entry point.

decisions.title: A site-specific parser
decisions.detail: Pairing adjacent rows is simple and matches the expected page structure. It also makes the scraper sensitive to changes in that HTML layout.

decisions.title: Keep scheduling claims separate
decisions.detail: The published entry point performs one run. Scheduling can be supplied externally, but the script is not a distributed crawling service or a built-in scheduler.

contracts.name: scrape_new_job_listings()
contracts.detail: Returns structured listing dictionaries or an empty result.

contracts.name: title / department / closing_date / summary
contracts.detail: Retains the information needed to compose a useful report.

scope: A targeted automation script. It does not establish multi-node crawling, durable deduplication, or delivery guarantees.

summary: An offline-capable chat application with React, Dexie/IndexedDB, authenticated FastAPI WebSockets, queued server processing, room delivery, and reconciliation APIs.

architecture.title: Local-first message state
architecture.detail: Dexie stores messages with pending, synced, or failed status and temp IDs. The frontend persists outgoing messages while offline and attempts reconciliation when connectivity returns.

architecture.title: Connection-aware delivery
architecture.detail: The FastAPI ConnectionManager maps users to multiple connection IDs, tracks room membership, queues message work, and handles chat, read receipts, and call-signaling events.

architecture.title: Reconciliation path
architecture.detail: POST /sync accepts offline messages, returns temp-to-server ID mappings, and retrieves up to 100 new messages from the user’s rooms since a supplied sync time.

decisions.title: Delivery and storage are distinct
decisions.detail: A WebSocket gives timely updates, while IndexedDB and the sync API preserve local work across disconnects. Client synchronization errors use exponential backoff capped at 30 seconds.

decisions.title: Deduplication is currently heuristic
decisions.detail: The sync endpoint checks matching sender, room, and content within a two-second window. That is a practical heuristic, not a durable idempotency-key guarantee.

contracts.name: WebSocket /ws/chat
contracts.detail: Carries chat messages, read receipts, room joins, and signaling events.

contracts.name: POST /sync → temp_id / server_id / status
contracts.detail: Reconciles offline records with server-side messages.

scope: The connection manager uses in-process maps and queues. Scaling delivery across multiple backend instances requires an additional shared coordination or fanout layer.

summary: The original FastAPI and SQLAlchemy content service, retained as a project after the website migrated to static JSON, prerendered pages, and direct email contact.

architecture.title: Content routes
architecture.detail: FastAPI routers separate portfolio items, blog posts, and contact submissions. Models represent each of those content types.

architecture.title: SQL persistence
architecture.detail: SQLAlchemy sessions use the mssql+pyodbc dialect and an ODBC SQL Server driver to access Azure SQL. Contact records include creation time and email-sent state.

architecture.title: Completed frontend migration
architecture.detail: The current website reads profile and journal JSON from its repository, generates static article and project pages, and uses email links for contact. It no longer calls this service.

decisions.title: Static content removes a runtime dependency
decisions.detail: Content changes now travel through Git review and the existing build/deploy workflow. The live site stays readable when the original API is unavailable.

decisions.title: Retirement preserves records
decisions.detail: The website’s 30 journals and original public project records were exported before database access was disabled. Existing private contact records remain in the retained database.

contracts.name: /portfolio / /blog / /contact
contracts.detail: The original router boundaries for content and submissions.

contracts.name: profile.json / journals.json
contracts.detail: The replacement content sources for the current website.

scope: An archived API, not the current website’s backend. Its database network access is disabled; the database remains retained rather than deleted.

summary: A location-privacy experiment that clusters visit history, identifies frequently visited places, perturbs sensitive coordinates, and overrides browser geolocation methods.

architecture.title: History-based sensitivity
architecture.detail: GeoGuardPrivacy reads JSON location history, standardizes coordinates, and uses DBSCAN to identify clusters. Visit counts determine which clusters qualify as points of interest.

architecture.title: Distance and perturbation
architecture.detail: The implementation uses Haversine calculations for cluster radii and checks whether a coordinate is near a sensitive place before selecting a privacy level.

architecture.title: Browser integration
architecture.detail: The extension wraps getCurrentPosition, watchPosition, and clearWatch and uses page messages to request privacy-preserving location responses.

decisions.title: Sensitivity comes from repeated visits
decisions.detail: The model treats frequently visited clusters differently from sparse or noisy points. Default clustering uses eps 0.1 and min_samples 3 after standardization.

decisions.title: Privacy requires more than moving a point
decisions.detail: Coordinate perturbation is the implemented mechanism. Its protection depends on the history, policy, browser integration, and the information a receiving application already has.

contracts.name: get_privacy_preserving_location(lat, lng)
contracts.detail: Returns a replacement coordinate pair for the configured privacy behavior.

contracts.name: GEO_GUARD_LOCATION_REQUEST / RESPONSE
contracts.detail: Connects the page-level geolocation wrapper with extension messaging.

scope: A geolocation privacy prototype. Perturbation and DBSCAN clustering do not establish a formal differential-privacy guarantee or an extension-wide security boundary.

summary: A Delphi/Pascal interpreter built around an ANTLR grammar and a Java parse-tree visitor with nested scopes, class definitions, object fields, and method metadata.

architecture.title: Grammar boundary
architecture.detail: delphi.g4 defines program structure, declarations, expressions, and class-related constructs. Generated lexer and parser classes turn source into a parse tree.

architecture.title: Visitor-based evaluation
architecture.detail: DelphiInterpreter extends delphiBaseVisitor<Object>. visitProgram pushes a global scope, visits declarations and the compound statement, then pops that scope.

architecture.title: Runtime structures
architecture.detail: Hash maps store classes, fields, methods, and visibility. A stack of scope maps and object instances carry execution state, including a this binding for method-related visits.

decisions.title: Syntax and runtime state are separate
decisions.detail: The grammar describes accepted structures; visitor methods interpret them. This keeps language recognition distinct from symbol and object handling.

decisions.title: The implementation follows the parse tree
decisions.detail: The public code uses an ANTLR parse-tree visitor. It does not show a separately constructed optimization-oriented AST or a native-code compiler backend.

contracts.name: DelphiInterpreter extends delphiBaseVisitor<Object>
contracts.detail: Defines the evaluation entry points used by the generated parser.

contracts.name: Stack<Map<String, Object>> scopes
contracts.detail: Represents nested environments separately from class definitions.

scope: An interpreter exploration of a Delphi/Pascal subset. Support should be assessed against the grammar and visitor implementation rather than assuming full language compatibility.
